title: Processes That Shape Earth's Surface
seo_title: Grade 7 Earth's Surface Worksheets: Fast and Slow Changes, Rates and Evidence
standard_text: Construct an explanation based on evidence for how geoscience processes have changed Earth's surface at varying time and spatial scales.
meta_desc: Free middle school science worksheets on processes that shape Earth's surface (NGSS MS-ESS2-2): fast events and slow processes, rates of erosion and uplift, and evidence in landforms. 100 practice questions with answers.
key_big: Small, slow changes add up to big landforms.
key_sub: Earthquakes and landslides change the land fast; rivers, glaciers and moving plates change it slowly over millions of years.
body_html:
How to think about it

Earth's surface is shaped by processes that work at very different time scales and spatial scales.

  • Fast and local: earthquakes, landslides, volcanic eruptions, flash floods, meteor impacts.
  • Slow and large: mountain building, rivers carving canyons, glaciers carving valleys, continents drifting.

Slow processes can make huge changes because tiny changes add up: 5 mm per year for 1,000,000 years is 5,000 meters. Evidence in landforms (fossils, rock layers, scratches from glaciers) helps explain how the surface changed.

Example

A river deepens its canyon 2 mm per year. How much in 1,000,000 years?

2 mm × 1,000,000 = 2,000,000 mm

= 2,000 m

Answer: 2,000 m

Example

Is a landslide fast or slow?

It happens in minutes.

Answer: fast

Common mistakes

  • Thinking all landforms formed quickly.
  • Thinking slow processes cannot make big changes.
  • Mixing up mm, cm and m when calculating over long times.

faq.q: What are examples of fast and slow changes to Earth's surface?
faq.a: Fast: earthquakes, landslides, eruptions and floods. Slow: mountain building, canyon carving by rivers, glaciers and continental drift.

faq.q: How can slow processes create huge landforms?
faq.a: Tiny changes each year add up over millions of years. A few millimeters a year can become kilometers.

faq.q: How do scientists know how Earth's surface changed?
faq.a: They use evidence such as rock layers, fossils, glacier scratches, matching coastlines and measurements of today's rates.

items.q: How can slow processes make large changes to Earth's surface?
c: Small changes add up over millions of years.
Slow processes only work on Mars.
items.e: 1 mm a year for a million years is 1 km.
